correctness.rationale: For each alpha>1, rational disk heights a_j=1/floor(j^alpha) eventually have gap a_j-a_{j+1} ~ alpha j^{-alpha-1}, so at mesh c/N they have matching packing/cover orders N^{1/(alpha+1)}. Each disk rotation frequency equals height a, giving |e^{2pi ita}-e^{2pi itb}|<=2pi t|a-b|. A height net at O(1/N) mesh and a fixed planar epsilon-net give an N-step Bowen spanning bound O(N^{1/(alpha+1)}) for X; ordered n-point products and Hausdorff factor give upper exponent n/(alpha+1). For lower bound, mark each of n points by fixed distinct radii r_i=i/(n+1) and select independently from cN^{1/(alpha+1)} heights spaced >=1/N and <=1/8. A changed ith height delta gives integer t=ceil(1/(4delta))<N with tdelta in [1/4,3/8], so same-radius chord separation >=sqrt(2)r_i, while different radii are always distance >=1/(n+1); thus (N,Delta)-separation of >=c^n N^{n/(alpha+1)} unlabeled configurations. Each configuration remains >=Delta/2 from singleton stratum; the quotient metric min(d,distA+distB) retains separation for n>=2. Full compact hyperspace contains F_n for all n, hence infinite polynomial entropy. Each finite subset is periodic (LCM of finitely many rational rotations), and bounded polynomial growth implies zero ordinary entropy. Independent exact-rational gap/phase checks at alpha=2,N=1000,10000,100000 corroborated the scale and tdelta inequalities; infinite assertions use the analytic proof, not samples.
